53-037.r: Zaid crops grown mainly in irrigated areas → Moong and Urad.

53-038.r: Zaid crop → Fodder (also watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, gourd, vegetables); gram and mustard → Rabi; cotton → Kharif.

53-039.r: Transplanted crop → Rice (paddy): needs less seed but more labour; helps weed control in wet, puddled fields.

53-040.r: All pairs correct when asked (answer e): Rice → West Bengal; Wheat → UP; Cotton → Gujarat; Mustard → Rajasthan. Now (2024-25): UP leads rice; Maharashtra leads cotton.

53-041.r: Rice 2018-19 ascending order: no option correct (answer e). Top rice states 2024-25: Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, West Bengal, Punjab, Chhattisgarh.

53-042.r: Rice ascending (when asked): Andhra Pradesh, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal. In 2024-25: Andhra Pradesh < Punjab < West Bengal < Uttar Pradesh.

53-043.r: Not helpful in nitrogen fixation → Paddy; gram, pea and bean help fix nitrogen.

53-044.r: Not a cash crop → Jowar; jute, sugarcane and groundnut are cash crops.

53-045.r: Kharif area: rice highest (51.27 million ha, 2024-25); cotton more than sugarcane; jowar (4.0) far below oilseeds (30.44); sugarcane not steadily falling → answer 1 and 3.

54-001.r: Cotton → subtropical, hurt by frost; needs 210 frost-free days, 50-100 cm rain, light well-drained moisture-holding soil; suits Deccan black cotton soil.

54-002.r: Cotton → mostly a Kharif cash crop; moderate rain 50-75 cm (R.C. Tiwari; others say 70-120 cm); frost harmful; semi-arid → both statements true.

54-003.r: Millet group → Sorghum, Kodo, Kangani, Ragi; groups with Maize or Moong are wrong. Millets: nutritious, drought-tolerant, grown in arid and semi-arid areas.

54-004.r: Largest cotton-producing area (when asked) → North-western and western India; cotton area in 2024-25: 11.48 million ha.

54-005.r: Largest cotton producer → Maharashtra; then Gujarat, Telangana (2024-25).

54-006.r: 'White Gold' districts of Madhya Pradesh (cotton) → Khandwa-Khargone.

54-007.r: 'White Gold' of Maharashtra → Cotton (grown on black soil).

54-008.r: India → original home of cotton (mentioned in Rigveda, Manusmriti) and first country to develop a hybrid cotton variety → both true.

54-009.r: Cotton fibres → obtained from the seed.

54-010.r: Maharashtra black-soil region: cotton losing to sugarcane → expanded irrigation makes the more profitable sugarcane possible.

54-011.r: Highest average cotton yield (when asked) → Andhra Pradesh; in 2024-25 → Odisha.

54-012.r: Largest number of cotton textile mills (among options) → Maharashtra (Ministry of Textiles Annual Report 2024-25).

55-001.r: Least water-efficient crop → Sugarcane (needs the most water); compared with sunflower, pearl millet, red gram.

55-002.r: Largest sugarcane area → Uttar Pradesh (2.72 million ha, 2024-25), then Maharashtra (1.17 million ha).

55-003.r: Highest irrigated share of crop area → Sugarcane 96.8% (2023-24); wheat 95.5%, rice 69.5%, oilseeds 43.9%.

55-004.r: Sugarcane producers when asked (descending): Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh; UP leads (also in 2024-25).

55-006.r: Largest sugarcane producers (among options) → Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. 2013 order: UP, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Haryana. 2024-25: UP, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat lead.

55-008.r: Molasses → by-product of sugar making (used for alcohol); bagasse → boiler fuel in sugar mills; sugar also from beetroot → answer 1 and 2.

55-009.r: Sustainable Sugarcane Initiative (WWF-ICRISAT, 2009) → fewer seeds, nursery seedlings, wide spacing, drip irrigation, more intercropping; chemical fertilizers still used (answer 1, 2, 4).

55-010.r: Sucrose in sugarcane falls → if frost occurs during ripening. Sugarcane suits 21-27°C and 75-100 cm rain.

55-011.r: Top three sugar producers when asked: UP, Maharashtra, Karnataka. Now (ISMA, 31 December 2025): Maharashtra first, UP second.

55-012.r: Sugar production 2015-16 (descending): Maharashtra, UP, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu; ISMA (December 2025): Maharashtra still first, UP second.

55-013.r: Sugar industry: India over 15% of world sugar, 2nd largest agro-based industry (after cotton), biggest consumer → 1, 2, 3 true. Largest producer is Brazil, not India.

55-014.r: Sakkar Nagar → sugar-producing centre in Andhra Pradesh (now Telangana).

55-016.r: 'Sugar Bowl' of India → Uttar Pradesh; now (31 December 2025) the second largest sugar producer.

55-017.r: First sugar mill in India → 1903 at Pratappur, Deoria district, Uttar Pradesh.

55-018.r: Sugar industry's shift North → South: higher cane yield per acre, higher sucrose content, longer crushing season (answer 1, 2, 3); cheap labour not counted.

55-019.r: Sugarcane breeding → Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu), set up 1912 under ICAR.

55-020.r: Sugarcane seeds → Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore; set up 1912 under ICAR.

55-021.r: Adsali sugarcane → planted July-August in low-rainfall Maharashtra; ripens in 16-18 months (answer: 18 months).

55-022.r: Sugar industry more developed in South India → higher cane yield per hectare and more juice → A and R true; R explains A.

55-023.r: UP: more sugarcane and sugar than Maharashtra but lower productivity (A true); Maharashtra's mills mostly cooperative (R true); R does not explain A.

56-001.r: Oilseed crop → Sunflower. Indian oilseeds: groundnut, mustard, coconut, soyabean, castor, cotton seed, linseed, sunflower.

56-002.r: Yellow Revolution → oilseeds; Green → foodgrain; White → milk; Blue → fish.

56-005.r: Most suitable dryland-farming crop → Groundnut (tropical, long warm season, 50-125 cm well-distributed rain).

56-006.r: Pegging → groundnut: after fertilization the faded flower's peg enters the soil and grows into a peanut.

56-007.r: Leading soyabean producer (when asked) → Madhya Pradesh. 2024-25: Maharashtra 7.37, Madhya Pradesh 5.38, Rajasthan 1.18 million tonnes.

56-010.r: Largest soyabean area → Madhya Pradesh: 48.642 lakh ha, 42.46% of India's soyabean area (SOPA 2025).

56-011.r: Record oilseed output 1992-93 → 20.11 million tonnes; again 2010-11 → 32.48 Mt; 2024-25 → 42.99 Mt.

56-012.r: Largest oilseed producer (when asked, 2018-19) → Madhya Pradesh; in 2024-25 → Rajasthan.
